Finding Summary: Entire KYC submission pipeline is mocked. AuthBloc receives SubmitKycPersonalDetailsUseCase, UploadKycDocumentUseCase, UploadKycSelfieUseCase, GetKycStatusUseCase in its constructor but never assigns or calls them. _onKycPersonalDetails, _onKycDocument, _onKycSelfie, _onKycStatusPoll all emit hardcoded success/pending states and ignore the event payload entirely (name, DOB, address, file paths, document type are never read or sent).
Impact: kyc_selfie_screen.dart shows the user a genuine 'Identity Verified — your identity has been successfully verified' dialog off a fake local state. No document or selfie is ever transmitted to the backend. This is a blocking compliance/production defect — users believe they are KYC-verified when no verification occurred.
Recommendation: Wire the four KYC use cases into the bloc for real; remove the hardcoded emits; do not show any 'verified' UI until a real server response confirms status. Treat as release blocker.

Finding Summary: Token-refresh has no mutex/dedup. When N parallel requests receive 401 simultaneously, each interceptor invocation independently reads the refresh token and calls /refresh with no in-flight lock.
Impact: If the backend rotates refresh tokens (single-use), only the first refresh succeeds and the remaining N-1 fail, force-logging-out a session that was still valid. Even without rotation, this wastes N refresh calls and races writing tokens back to storage, risking a stale token winning the write.
Recommendation: Introduce a single shared in-flight refresh Future/Completer that all concurrent 401 handlers await instead of each independently calling /refresh.

Finding Summary: No BLoC event handler uses droppable()/sequential() EventTransformer (default is unbounded concurrent). Every screen instead relies on a client-side 'if (state is AuthLoading) return;' guard, which is a TOCTOU race: it reads state synchronously but emit(AuthLoading()) only lands after the event is asynchronously dequeued, so a fast double-tap can pass the guard twice. sso_set_password_screen.dart has no guard at all.
Impact: Double-tap on Login, Register, Send OTP, Resend OTP, Forgot Password, and SSO Set Password can each fire two concurrent network calls whose responses can resolve out of order, causing duplicate submissions, double account actions, or an inconsistent final UI state.
Recommendation: Apply bloc_concurrency's droppable() (or sequential() where order matters) to every on<Event>() registration instead of relying on ad hoc state checks in the UI.

Finding Summary: _onSetSsoPassword silently no-ops if the bloc's mutable _currentUser field is null when the setPassword call succeeds — no error and no state is emitted.
Impact: UI is left stuck on AuthLoading indefinitely (spinner forever) whenever _currentUser has been nulled by a race with logout or a bloc recreation before this screen completes.
Recommendation: Never branch success handling on mutable instance state; derive user identity from the event/response, or emit an explicit error/recovery state when the expected context is missing.

Finding Summary: AuthRemoteDataSourceImpl does deep unsafe casts on server responses (e.g. (response.data['data'] as Map<String,dynamic>)['data'] as Map<String,dynamic>). A failed cast throws a Dart TypeError, which is an Error not an Exception, so AuthRepositoryImpl's 'on Exception catch (e)' (used in 10 of 11 repo methods) does not catch it. Only _onLogin in the bloc has a bare catch(e) backstop; every other handler (register, verifyOtp, resendOtp, sendOtp, SSO send/verify, setPassword, checkEmailExists, forgotPassword, logout, all KYC) has no try/catch.
Impact: A malformed or unexpected server response shape leaves the bloc stuck in AuthLoading indefinitely for nearly every auth action except login — the app appears to hang with no error and no way to retry short of restarting.
Recommendation: Catch Object/Error at the repository boundary (not just Exception), or validate/parse response shapes defensively and map any failure to a Failure type consistently across every repo method.

Finding Summary: uploadKycDocument / uploadKycSelfie call MultipartFile.fromFile() directly with no file-size cap and no MIME/extension check.
Impact: A 20+MB camera photo (or an arbitrary non-image file picked via gallery) uploads in full over any network with no client-side warning, wasting bandwidth/time on poor connections and allowing unexpected file types to reach the backend.
Recommendation: Validate file size and MIME type/extension client-side before upload; reject or compress oversized images with clear user feedback.

Finding Summary: saveUser/getUser store the full user object (email, full name, KYC status) via jsonEncode into plain SharedPreferences, while tokens correctly use flutter_secure_storage. Inconsistent security posture despite flutter_secure_storage/encrypt already being project dependencies.
Impact: PII is trivially recoverable from an unencrypted device backup or on a rooted/jailbroken device, even though the token storage on the same screen is hardened.
Recommendation: Store the cached user object in flutter_secure_storage (or encrypt it before writing to SharedPreferences) for consistency with token handling.

Finding Summary: EmailNotVerifiedException is rethrown raw through AuthRepositoryImpl.login and LoginUseCase (neither has a try/catch for it), breaking the Either<Failure,...> contract used everywhere else. It relies entirely on the bloc's outer try/catch in _onLogin to catch it. ErrorHandler.mapExceptionToFailure's switch does not include this exception type at all.
Impact: This is the single place in the codebase where an exception crosses the Either boundary instead of being mapped to a Failure. If _onLogin's catch block is ever refactored or the transformer changed, this silently falls through and either crashes the handler or gets mis-mapped to UnknownFailure.
Recommendation: Map EmailNotVerifiedException to a proper Failure type inside the repository (or add it to ErrorHandler.mapExceptionToFailure) so login follows the same Either contract as every other auth operation.

Finding Summary: _currentUser is imperative mutable state on a @singleton bloc, read/written outside of `state`, rather than derived from the BLoC's own emitted state.
Impact: Root cause of F-04; also a stale-session-bleed-through risk — e.g. an in-flight SSO/KYC continuation can read _currentUser after a concurrent logout has already nulled it, or after a different user has since logged in.
Recommendation: Fold _currentUser into the state class itself (e.g. carried on the relevant state variants) so it can't go stale independent of the emitted state stream.

Finding Summary: The dedicated RateLimitFailure countdown widget described in RATE_LIMIT_HANDLING.md is not wired into any auth screen — all screens show RateLimitFailure via a plain generic AppSnackbar.showError(). The independent client-side 30s OTP-resend cooldown timer is not synced to the server's actual Retry-After value, so the two can disagree.
Impact: User can be shown 'you can resend now' by the client timer while the server still rejects with 429, producing a confusing repeat failure and no visible countdown.
Recommendation: Wire the existing RateLimitFailure countdown widget into every screen that can receive it, and initialize/resync the client cooldown timer from the server's Retry-After header on every response.

Finding Summary: KycLoading is defined and referenced in all three KYC screens' isLoading checks, but the bloc never emits it anywhere.
Impact: Currently a dead state; once F-01 is fixed and real network calls are wired in, KYC screens still won't show a loading indicator or block double submission unless this state is actually emitted during the real async calls.
Recommendation: Emit KycLoading at the start of each real KYC handler once F-01 is fixed, and ensure it is cleared consistently.

Finding Summary: _submit() trusts _emailExists == true without re-checking that _checkedEmail still equals the current text field value. Only the submit button's disabled-state computation re-validates freshness of the check.
Impact: An Enter-key / onFieldSubmitted path that bypasses the disabled button can act on a stale email-exists result for a previously-typed email address if the user edits the field after the debounce fires but before submitting via keyboard.
Recommendation: Re-validate _checkedEmail == current field value inside _submit() itself, not only in the button's enabled/disabled computation.

Finding Summary: LoginFormManager is a bare singleton holding raw TextEditingController/FocusNode references from whichever screen last registered them. clearForm() (called from otp_verification_screen.dart's _backToLogin) can run against already-disposed controllers if navigation/dispose ordering races with unregisterControllers().
Impact: Potential 'used after dispose' exception on rapid back-navigation from the OTP screen to Login, depending on widget dispose ordering.
Recommendation: Guard clearForm() with disposed-state checks, or move controller ownership out of a bare singleton into a properly scoped provider tied to widget lifecycle.

Finding Summary: logout() swallows all remote logout failures (catch (_) {}) before clearing local state. Reasonable as a best-effort UX fallback, but undocumented and untested anywhere.
Impact: If the remote /logout call never reaches the backend (network failure), tokens can remain valid server-side even though the app has locally 'successfully' logged the user out, with no record of this discrepancy.
Recommendation: Document this as an intentional best-effort behavior, and/or surface a non-blocking warning when the remote call fails so it's at least observable/loggable.

Finding Summary: ~350 and ~170 lines of dead, commented-out prior implementations left in these two screens respectively.
Impact: Increases file size/noise, risks a stale implementation being accidentally re-enabled or confusing future maintainers about which code path is live.
Recommendation: Delete dead commented-out code; rely on git history for prior implementations.

Finding Summary: _emailDebounce?.cancel() is called twice in dispose() (duplicate line).
Impact: Harmless (cancel is idempotent) but indicates copy-paste residue.

Finding Summary: No upload-progress feedback is surfaced for KYC document/selfie uploads.
Impact: Once F-01 is fixed and real (potentially large) file uploads occur, users on slow connections get no progress indicator, only an indefinite spinner.
Recommendation: Surface Dio upload progress (onSendProgress) as a percentage/progress bar once real uploads are wired in.

File:Line: send_otp_usecase.dart; resend_otp_usecase.dart; send_sso_login_otp_usecase.dart; set_password_usecase.dart; forgot_password_usecase.dart; logout_usecase.dart
Finding Summary: sendOtp/resendOtp/sendSsoLoginOtp/setPassword return Either<Failure, Unit> while forgotPassword/logout return Either<Failure, String>, with no clear behavioral reason for the difference.
Impact: Minor inconsistency that makes the use case layer's contract less predictable for future maintainers extending the auth flow.
Recommendation: Standardize on one return convention (e.g. Unit for side-effect-only calls, a typed result only where the message is actually used) across all auth use cases.
